newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon growth slows in February.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon growth slows in February.

text.p: Lebanon's economic activity fell in February to its lowest level in 10 months and the Bank of Lebanon said on Tuesday the slowdown was partly due to seasonal factors.
Construction declined sharply with permits falling 47.5 percent on a year-on-year basis and cement deliveries down 24.7 percent, the bank said in its latest economic bulletin.

Meanwhile, public debt continued to soar. The bank said net total public debt rose to 16,913 billion pounds ($10.913 billion) from 16,471 billion pounds in January for an annual growth of 39.20 percent.

The bank said its coincident indicator of economic activity -- which it publishes in the absence of official economic growth statistics -- fell to 161.4 in February from 166.0 in January and compared with 150.2 in February 1996.
It was the lowest level since April 1996 when the indicator stood at 150.1.
The bank said the figures suggested a slowdown in economic activity "in part due to seasonal factors".

"During February, construction activity was sluggish while tourism increased in response to the February Shopping Month initiative," the bank said. Many shops and hotels gave 50 percent discounts in February in a government-sponsored initiative to stimulate commerce and foreign tourism.
Passenger arrivals and departures at Beirut International Airport surged by 31.5 percent in February compared with February 1996, the bank said.
Lebanon's balance of payments registered a surplus of $24 million in February, bringing the total surplus since the beginning of the year to $227 million.

"This surplus was reflected in the rise in net foreign assets of the central bank by $514 million, while the banks' net foreign assets fell by $287 million due to a continuing shift towards the Lebanese pound," the bank said.
The January balance of trade deficit widened to $507.8 million from $426 million in January.
Imports rose by 10.5 percent to $571.3 million from a year earlier while exports declined by 8.3 percent to $63.5 million, the bank said.
The foreign debt rose to $1.829 billion from $1.822 billion in January.
